excerpts.text: With some receiving the Nobel Prize more than once, this makes a total of 892 individuals (including 844 men, 48 women) and 24 organizations.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-8) Six Nobel laureates were not permitted by their governments to accept the Nobel Prize. [Adolf Hitler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Hitler "Adolf Hitler") forbade four Germans, [Richard Kuhn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Kuhn "Richard Kuhn") (Chemistry, 1938), [Adolf Butenandt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Butenandt "Adolf Butenandt") (Chemistry, 1939), [Gerhard Domagk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerhard_Domagk "Gerhard Domagk") (Physiology or Medicine, 1939) and [Carl von Ossietzky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_von_Ossietzky "Carl von Ossietzky") (Peace, 1936) from accepting their Nobel Prizes.

Among the 892 Nobel laureates, 48 have been women; the first woman to receive a Nobel Prize was [Marie Curie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_Curie "Marie Curie"), who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-WomenLaureates-12) She was also the first person to be awarded two Nobel Prizes, the second award being the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, given in 1911.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates#cite_note-NobelFacts-11)
